title: U.S. House · Florida's 13th District
area: West-central Florida, including parts of Pinellas County around St. Petersburg and Clearwater.

context.text: The Republican primary was canceled and incumbent Anna Paulina Luna advanced unopposed. Leela Gray won the Democratic primary with 65.1% of the vote against Brandt Robinson and John Liccione.

candidates.name: Anna Paulina Luna

summary.text: Anna Paulina Luna is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election to Florida's 13th Congressional District. A U.S. Air Force veteran, she previously worked in conservative media and advocacy before her election to Congress in 2022.

background.text: Born in Orange, California in 1989; served in the U.S. Air Force from 2009 to 2018.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of West Florida in 2017.
Worked as an entrepreneur, director of Hispanic engagement for Turning Point USA, chairwoman of Hispanic initiative for PragerU, and a podcast host with Gingrich 360 before entering Congress.

priorities.text: Immigration: says she will fight to finish the border wall, end DACA, restore the Remain in Mexico policy, and oppose amnesty as a pathway to citizenship.
priorities.quote: Anna will fight to finish the border wall, end DACA, restore President Trump’s Remain in Mexico policy, and crack down on criminal illegals in America.

priorities.text: Education: says she will work to expand school choice, ensure parental rights, and protect women's sports.
priorities.quote: Anna will work to advance efforts to expand school choice, ensure parents rights, protect women’s sports, and increase civic literacy.

priorities.text: Government accountability: says she will support a ban on members of Congress and staff becoming lobbyists after leaving office and push to enact term limits for elected officials.
priorities.quote: She will support any ban on Congress or its employees becoming lobbyists to cash out after leaving office. She will also work to enact term limits for elected officials.

positions.summary: Cosponsored H.R. 22, the SAVE Act, and H.R. 7296, the SAVE America Act (119th Congress).

record.text: Assigned to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation; Health Care and Financial Services; Military and Foreign Affairs subcommittees) and the Committee on Foreign Affairs for the 2025-2026 Congress.

candidates.researchNotes: Luna has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; positions and priorities are drawn from her official House issues pages, which cover only a subset of the 15 tracked issues.

candidates.name: Leela Gray

summary.text: Leela Gray is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 13th Congressional District. A retired U.S. Army Brigadier General with 30 years of service, she is running on affordability, government ethics, and support for veterans and seniors.

background.text: Says her family relied on food stamps growing up and that she worked two jobs to pay for college before joining the U.S. Army.
Served 30 years in the U.S. Army, rising to the rank of Brigadier General.

priorities.text: Affordability: says she would crack down on corporations and insurance monopolies driving up costs, expand affordable housing, make healthcare more competitive and transparent, and provide tax relief to middle-class families and small businesses rather than "the ultra-wealthy and big corporations."
Government ethics: says she would push to ban insider stock trading by members of Congress, enact term limits, and impose a lifetime lobbying ban on former members.
Veterans and seniors: says she would cut red tape at the VA and work to protect and strengthen Social Security and Medicare.

positions.summary: Says on her campaign site that she is running to end the tariffs.
positions.quote: I am running to put an end to the tariff taxes raising the cost of groceries, building materials and everyday goods

positions.summary: Says she will fight for a tax code that asks the wealthiest to pay more.
positions.quote: I will fight for a tax code that asks the wealthiest to pay their fair share

statements.quote: We must restore the ACA tax credits Luna allowed to expire, cap out-of-pocket costs for essential medications, protect Medicare's power to negotiate lower prices
statements.context: On her campaign website, Cutting Costs Agenda

statements.quote: We also must commit to making childcare affordable and homeownership attainable, ensuring the next generation has better opportunities.
statements.context: On her campaign website, Growing Economic Opportunities

statements.quote: We need to permanently ban offshore drilling and protect all our homes, businesses, and coastal economy.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements are from the issue pages of her campaign website (leelagray.com) and her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. No specific statements on abortion, guns, immigration or policing were found on the site.

candidates.name: Tony D'Arrigo

summary.text: Tony D'Arrigo is running with no party affiliation for Florida's 13th Congressional District in the November 3, 2026 general election.

priorities.text: Healthcare: calls it the most important issue facing the district and says he supports expanding coverage, protecting the ACA and de-privatizing hospitals.
Housing: proposes increasing affordable housing supply, tenant safeguards and government-backed mortgages capped at 5%.
Campaign finance: pledges to refuse dark money and to accept only contributions that can be tracked and traced.

positions.summary: Says on his campaign site that he supports universal healthcare coverage, and in a Tampa Bay 28 questionnaire that he supports expanding coverage and protecting the ACA.
positions.quote: Healthcare isn't just a privilege—it's a fundamental right.

positions.summary: Lists zoning reforms among his housing proposals.
positions.quote: Champion fast-track incentives, zoning reforms, and public-private partnerships to build more affordable homes and apartments

positions.summary: Lists tenant safeguards against evictions and rent increases among his housing proposals.
positions.quote: Advocate for tenant safeguards to prevent unjust evictions and excessive rent hikes, without overburdening responsible landlords.

positions.summary: Proposes redirecting oil and gas subsidies to renewable energy.
positions.quote: Reallocate oil and gas industry subsidies to invest in renewable energy—solar, wind, hydrogen, and beyond.

candidates.researchNotes: From his campaign website (home and Platform pages) and Tampa Bay 28 questionnaire. The site also contains statements about opponents and parties that are not reproduced. No statements found on abortion, policing or school choice.

statements.quote: I will fight for a practical, effective resolution to gun violence
statements.context: On his campaign website, Platform page
